contexts.text: To suck the milk of the gentiles, and the breasts of kings () = to be endowed with goods and instructed in truths. ( = the insinuation of celestial good and celestial truth. AC 6745:3.) AE 175:3.
A species of suction or drawing induced on the head by Spirits. Described. SE 1128. SE 1129.
The infants, and those that suck the breasts () = the innocent.
To suck honey out of the rock () = the delight from memory truths. AE 314:7. AE 374:10. AE 411:7.

To suck the affluence of the sea () = that they will then imbibe memory truth in abundance, or that it will be insinuated. To suck, here, is the same word as to be suckled in the following places. Illustrated. AC 6762. AE 445:5.
To suck oil out of the flint of rock () = to be imbued with good through the truths of faith.
An infant knows only how to suck, (which) it has imbibed from the continual suction in the womb. TCR 335:7.
Said they would suck out the marrows.
They suck out such things from (those) with whom they are.
He wanted to suck out my blood.
To suck () = influx from the Lord.
The suckling, or suckling infant () = the good of innocence. AE 581:5.
